title: AMQP 1.0 specification test vector
description: One NDJSON line of a specification test vector. Vectors are authored from OASIS clauses or from recorded third-party exchanges, never produced by running the executable specification (PLAN.md §5 rule 2), and replay uses logical time only: `tick` steps are ordering tags, never wall-clock readings, so a replay is deterministic on any machine. The executable specification (S1 onward) consumes this format and reports a verdict per vector, naming the error condition it expects for negative vectors.

vector.description: Stable identifier, unique within the corpus. Appears in dispositions and coverage reports, so it is part of the contract.

kind.description: positive: must be admitted, with the named outputs. negative: must be rejected with the named error condition. recorded: captured from a third-party implementation and used to test the specification's adequacy.

role.description: The role the endpoint under test plays. The specification binds roles on both sides of the version negotiation, so a vector without a role is under-specified.

clauses.description: Clause ids this vector is testing, as they appear in ledger/clauses.json. The coverage report cross-checks these against the ledger, so vectors cannot accumulate free of the clauses they claim to exercise.

config.description: Negotiable values in force for this vector. Absent fields take the value the specification declares as a default, which is generated, not transcribed.

outcome.description: The outcome the endpoint is configured to send, where a clause lets it choose.

provenance.description: Required for kind=recorded, and forbidden otherwise: a clause-authored vector cites clauses, an observed one cites the implementation it observed.

peer.description: The implementation observed, e.g. "Apache Qpid Proton".

method.description: All third-party vectors are captures; a synthesised third-party vector would be a fabrication.

recorder.description: Who captured it: the reviewer must be able to ask them how.

transcriptSha256.description: Digest of the full session transcript kept out of tree. Establishes that the steps are an excerpt of a real exchange rather than a construction.

expectError.description: Required for kind=negative: "it fails" is not a specification. A mandated refusal names the error condition and the endpoint that must close.

condition.description: An error-condition symbol from the generated table, e.g. amqp:connection:framing-error.

clause.description: The clause that mandates this refusal, when the vector tests a refusal rather than a decode error.

steps.description: The exchange. Steps are ordered; nothing is implied by position beyond that ordering.

dir.description: in: peer to endpoint. out: endpoint to peer.

bytes.description: Frame bytes, lowercase hex, no separators. For dir=out with expect=bytes this is the required exact output; the specification fixes those bytes.

expect.description: bytes: the endpoint's output is fixed octet-for-octet. action: the specification permits latitude (fragmentation split points, credit values, ordering where a clause allows a choice) and the step names what must happen instead.

env.description: An environment event rather than an exchange: a logical tick, end of stream, or a partial read. Modelling these as explicit steps is what keeps replay deterministic.

tick.description: Logical milliseconds since the previous step. Never a wall-clock reading.

partial.description: Deliver only this many octets of the next available input, so a decoder's incremental behaviour is exercised.
